strings.name: Boris Johnson
strings.role: Politician · writer · former UK prime minister
strings.summary: Johnson moved from journalism into Parliament and served as London mayor, foreign secretary and prime minister. He helped lead the Brexit campaign and oversaw the UK’s EU withdrawal. His government faced COVID-19 and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Lockdown-party and integrity controversies undermined his leadership; a 2023 Commons committee found deliberate misleading of Parliament. He disputed the inquiry and left Parliament, continuing writing and public appearances.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A former UK prime minister who advanced Brexit, with wide influence through foreign policy, pandemic governance and political style.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: New York City, United States; his journalism and political career developed mainly in Britain.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Attended Eton College and Balliol College, Oxford, studying classics.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Brexit and government
strings.highlights.h1.text: Backed the 2016 Leave campaign, became prime minister in 2019 and oversaw formal EU withdrawal in 2020.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Political integrity controversy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Partygate and ministerial resignations preceded his departure; a Commons committee later found he deliberately misled Parliament.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Presented memoir in Lviv
strings.timeline.t1.text: Visited Lviv, Ukraine, to present the Ukrainian edition of Unleashed at a book festival.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Left Commons amid committee findings
strings.timeline.t2.text: Announced his resignation as an MP; the subsequent Privileges Committee report found deliberate misleading of the Commons.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Left Downing Street
strings.timeline.t3.text: Handed over to Liz Truss after losing ministerial support, ending three years as prime minister.
strings.timeline.t4.title: UK left the European Union
strings.timeline.t4.text: His government advanced the withdrawal agreement; the UK left the EU, with a separate transition ending in December.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became prime minister
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won the Conservative leadership and took office; his party won a Commons majority that December.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Became foreign secretary
strings.timeline.t6.text: Served under Theresa May, resigning in 2018 over Brexit policy.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Elected London mayor
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began two mayoral terms; London hosted the 2012 Olympics during his tenure.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First elected to Parliament
strings.timeline.t8.text: Elected for Henley; later represented Uxbridge and South Ruislip from 2015.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Entered journalism
strings.timeline.t9.text: Entered journalism after Oxford and later edited The Spectator.
